claims.body: The Canadiens are near the top of the league for chance quality, but the Avalanche are near the top at preventing dangerous shots. We think the Avalanche win this one.

claims.body: The Canadiens are around the middle of the league for shots from in close, and the Avalanche are the worst. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one. Shots from in close tend to be the more dangerous ones.

notes.text: Chris Kreider is out (lower body injury) and has missed the last 4 games.
Josh Anderson is out about 3-4 weeks (lower body injury) and has missed the last 3 games.

Mike Matheson is out about 3-4 weeks (lower body injury) and has missed the last 4 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Alexandre Carrier has taken his spot beside Kaiden Guhle. That pair has had 38% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 33:41 together, down from 54% with Matheson.
Brett Berard was added to the roster on Nov 16 and has played beside Oliver Kapanen and Owen Beck.
Oliver Kapanen is no longer killing penalties: 1% of the team’s shorthanded time in 16 games, down from 33% last season.
Arber Xhekaj has started killing penalties: on the ice for 29% of the team’s shorthanded time in 22 games, up from 6% last season.
Nathan MacKinnon is out (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 3 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Brock Nelson has taken his spot beside Artturi Lehkonen and Martin Nečas.

Cale Makar is on injured reserve and has missed the last 3 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Sam Malinski has taken his spot beside Devon Toews. That pair has had 65% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 39:52 together, about what it had with Makar (61%).
Mike Reilly was added to the roster on Nov 16.
Zachary L'Heureux is no longer killing penalties: 3% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, down from 36% with his old team last season.

stakes: The Canadiens go in tied for first in the Atlantic with 32 points, the Avalanche third in the Central with 29 points.

COL.head: The Avalanche should have the upper hand
COL.body: Even though Colorado will be without MacKinnon, the Avalanche have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. The Canadiens’ way back in is piling up shots.

MTL.head: The Canadiens face a real test
MTL.body: Even though Colorado will be without MacKinnon, the Avalanche have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. The Canadiens can pull it off if they keep the shots coming.

story.head: Suzuki’s favorite opponent
paras: The Avalanche won the teams’ first meeting this season, 4-1 in Montréal on Nov 14. The Avs (13-7-3) beat Anaheim 4-0 on Thursday, and the Canadiens have won two in a row. Two of the league’s best teams meet. Going in, the Canadiens are second in the Atlantic (tied for fourth in the NHL) and the Avalanche third in the Central (tied for tenth).

The Canadiens’ record (.696) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.548), largely because they’re 9-5 in one-goal games. The Avalanche’s record (.630) is about what their chances are worth.

The Canadiens get into more chippy games than almost anyone (2nd) and have had some of the best goaltending in the league (4th), but take more penalties than they draw (31st). The Avalanche play the league’s fastest games (1st) and get their defensemen shooting (2nd). They also do a lot of their shooting from distance (lowest), so the Canadiens have the edge over them on shots from in close. Colorado has scored 3.91 goals a game, the second most in the league. The Canadiens’ good looks will be harder to come by against the Avalanche.

Lane Hutson (5 G / 19 A / 24 P in 23 GP) leads the Canadiens in scoring, and Cole Caufield (12 G / 8 A / 20 P in 23 GP) has a team-high twelve goals. For the Avalanche, Martin Nečas (10 G / 16 A / 26 P in 23 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Artturi Lehkonen (15 G / 6 A / 21 P in 23 GP) has a team-high 15 goals, fifth in the NHL.
Jacob Fowler (10-2-2 / .924 SV% in 14 GS) has been terrific for Montréal and will likely start. Mackenzie Blackwood (11-4-1 / .904 SV% in 16 GS) is in line to start for Colorado.

items.text: Nick Suzuki has a point in seven straight games against Colorado.
The Canadiens are newly without Josh Anderson, and have been without Chris Kreider, Samuel Montembeault and Mike Matheson for several games. Jacob Fowler is expected to start.
The Avalanche are newly without Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, no team is missing more right now.
With Nathan MacKinnon out, Parker Kelly took eight faceoffs in the Avalanche’s last game. He had been taking about two a game.
